# Child acquisition curves include VO and VOO {#sec-curves}

{{< include _caution.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = Path("data")
META = pd.read_json(DATA / "summary.json", typ="series")
CURVES = pd.read_csv(DATA / "canvas_age_curves.csv")
ORDER = pd.read_csv(DATA / "canvas_order.csv")
AOA = pd.read_csv(DATA / "canvas_censored_aoa.csv")
FIRST = pd.read_csv(DATA / "first_ages.csv")
EXPOSURE = pd.read_csv(DATA / "token_exposure.csv")

TITLES = {
    "VL": "VL intransitive locative",
    "VOL": "VOL caused motion",
    "VO": "VO transitive",
    "VOO": "VOO ditransitive",
}
MIN_CHILDREN = {"VL": 10, "VOL": 10, "VO": 16, "VOO": 8}
VACS = ["VL", "VOL", "VO", "VOO"]

plt.rcParams.update({
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "figure.dpi": 120,
    "font.size": 10,
})

gold = int(META["parse_source_tokens"]["childesdb"])
silver = int(META["parse_source_tokens"]["stanza_gloss"])
n_corp = int(META["n_corpora"])
n_child = int(META["n_children"])
exp = EXPOSURE.set_index("age_months")["n_tokens"]
exp_lo, exp_hi = int(exp.min()), int(exp.max())
exp_lo_age, exp_hi_age = int(exp.idxmin()), int(exp.idxmax())
exp_sum = int(exp.sum())
child_tok = {k: int(v) for k, v in META["child_tokens"].items()}
```

Schematic VL, VOL, VO, and VOO on `{python} n_corp` English CHILDES corpora from `tokens_filled.parquet` (childes-db 2026.1 gold parses plus Stanza-on-gloss fills). Remaining fully unparsed utterances are dropped. Each panel shows the eight most frequent child-produced verbs in that construction. Line-chart CDFs are inverse-weighted by total child tokens in each age bin so corpus coverage does not set the shape. Locative verb+preposition series are in the CSV tables. Model epoch curves are not scored yet.

::: {.callout-note}
## Filled parses
Gold childes-db tags cover `{python} f"{gold:,}"` tokens; Stanza-on-gloss added `{python} f"{silver:,}"` tokens. Extraction keeps utterances with POS and `%gra` so silver fills are included and leftover unparsed speech is not.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## CDFs adjusted for sampling density
Child tokens (any word) per 3-month bin range from `{python} f"{exp_lo:,}"` (`{python} exp_lo_age` mo) to `{python} f"{exp_hi:,}"` (`{python} exp_hi_age` mo); `{python} f"{exp_sum:,}"` child tokens between 18 and 72 months. Each verb's CDF uses verb-tokens / all-tokens in that bin, then renormalizes, so the shape tracks the word rather than how much CHILDES data happens to exist.
:::

| Construction | Child tokens |
|---|---|
| VL | `{python} f"{child_tok['VL']:,}"` |
| VOL | `{python} f"{child_tok['VOL']:,}"` |
| VO | `{python} f"{child_tok['VO']:,}"` |
| VOO | `{python} f"{child_tok['VOO']:,}"` |

::: {.callout-note}
## VO and VOO are verb-level
Transitive VO and ditransitive VOO have no preposition grain. KM median first age: *want* 20 / *get* 21 months (VO). *give* 30 months (VOO; 281 producers). The 5-child earliest-median ranking on `{python} n_child` children is dominated by rare lemmas, so the plots use token-frequency occupants instead.
:::

## Sampling-adjusted CDFs

Each 3-month bin is weighted by this verb's tokens divided by all child tokens (any word) in that bin, then accumulated and renormalized to 100%. Lines are verbs produced by at least the construction-specific child minimum. Y-axis is cumulative weighted share (%).

```{python}
#| label: fig-cdf
#| fig-cap: "Sampling-adjusted cumulative token share by child age for the eight most frequent child-produced verbs in each schematic VAC."
#| fig-height: 8

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, vac in zip(axes.ravel(), VACS):
    order = ORDER.loc[ORDER.vac.eq(vac)]
    keep = set(order.loc[order.n_children >= MIN_CHILDREN[vac], "verb"])
    sub = CURVES.loc[CURVES.vac.eq(vac) & CURVES.verb.isin(keep)]
    verbs = order.loc[order.verb.isin(keep), "verb"]
    for verb in verbs:
        row = sub.loc[sub.verb.eq(verb)].sort_values("age_months")
        ax.plot(row.age_months, row.cumulative_share * 100, label=verb)
    ax.set_title(TITLES[vac])
    ax.set_xlim(18, 69)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right", frameon=False, ncol=2)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Cumulative weighted share (%)")
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("Cumulative weighted share (%)")
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Age (months)")
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel("Age (months)")
fig.tight_layout()
```

## First production by child, left-truncated and right-censored

Each small dot is one child's first observed use of that verb+construction. Children enter the risk set at their first recorded child-speech session (left truncation). A first use in that first session is left-censored (acquired at or before first observation) and counted at entry. Children who never produced the combination are right-censored at their last parsed child-speech session and are not plotted as dots. The large marker is the Kaplan–Meier median age of acquisition; whiskers are a 95% bootstrap CI. If the KM curve never falls to 50%, the median is not reached and a dashed arrow shows the lower bound (if any).

```{python}
#| echo: false

def swarm_y(ages, y0, bin_w=0.45, spread=0.32):
    keys = np.round(np.asarray(ages) / bin_w) * bin_w
    y = np.full(len(ages), float(y0))
    for k in np.unique(keys):
        idx = np.flatnonzero(keys == k)
        n = len(idx)
        if n < 2:
            continue
        step = min(0.05, (spread * 2) / (n - 1))
        y[idx] = y0 + (np.arange(n) - (n - 1) / 2) * step
    return y


def plot_km(ax, vac):
    aoa = AOA.loc[AOA.vac.eq(vac)].sort_values("aoa_rank")
    verbs = list(aoa.verb)
    ages = FIRST.loc[FIRST.vac.eq(vac)]
    for i, verb in enumerate(verbs):
        dots = ages.loc[ages.verb.eq(verb), "first_age"].to_numpy()
        ax.scatter(dots, swarm_y(dots, i), s=8, alpha=0.4, c="#2c7fb8", linewidths=0, zorder=2)
        row = aoa.iloc[i]
        km, lo, hi = row.km_median, row.km_ci_low, row.km_ci_high
        if pd.notna(km) and pd.notna(lo) and pd.notna(hi):
            ax.hlines(i, lo, hi, color="black", lw=1.6, zorder=3)
            ax.vlines([lo, hi], i - 0.18, i + 0.18, color="black", lw=1.6, zorder=3)
            ax.scatter([km], [i], s=36, c="black", zorder=4)
        elif pd.notna(lo):
            ax.annotate("", xy=(72, i), xytext=(lo, i),
                        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="black", lw=1.2, linestyle="--"))
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(verbs)), verbs)
    ax.set_xlim(18, 72)
    ax.set_ylim(len(verbs) - 0.6, -0.6)
    ax.set_title(TITLES[vac])
    ax.set_xticks([18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72])
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-km
#| fig-cap: "First observed production age (dots) with Kaplan–Meier median and 95% bootstrap CI (marker and whiskers). Verbs ordered by earliest KM median. Source: tokens_filled.parquet · 61 corpora · 962 children · childes-db 2026.1 + Stanza-on-gloss. Right-censored Kaplan–Meier with delayed entry."
#| fig-height: 9

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 9), sharex=True)
for ax, vac in zip(axes.ravel(), VACS):
    plot_km(ax, vac)
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel("Age (months)")
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel("Age (months)")
fig.tight_layout()
```

## Kaplan–Meier median first age

Same eight verbs as the plots above. Rank 1 = earliest KM median. Medians that are not reached (survival never falls to 50%) are listed last. The interval is a 95% bootstrap CI; a lower bound only means the median itself was not reached. Producers are children with an observed first use (`n_event`); never-producers are right-censored. Left truncation: children enter at first observation.

```{python}
#| echo: false

def km_table(vac):
    aoa = AOA.loc[AOA.vac.eq(vac)].sort_values("aoa_rank").copy()
    tok = ORDER.loc[ORDER.vac.eq(vac), ["verb", "n_tokens"]]
    out = aoa.merge(tok, on="verb")
    reached = out.median_reached.fillna(False).astype(bool) & out.km_median.notna()
    median = np.where(reached, out.km_median.map(lambda x: f"{x:.1f}"), "not reached")
    ci = []
    for _, r in out.iterrows():
        if pd.notna(r.km_ci_low) and pd.notna(r.km_ci_high):
            ci.append(f"{r.km_ci_low:.1f}–{r.km_ci_high:.1f}")
        elif pd.notna(r.km_ci_low):
            ci.append(f"≥ {r.km_ci_low:.1f}")
        else:
            ci.append("—")
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "Rank": range(1, len(out) + 1),
        "Verb": out.verb.to_numpy(),
        "KM median (mo)": median,
        "95% CI": ci,
        "Producers": out.n_event.astype(int).to_numpy(),
        "Tokens": out.n_tokens.astype(int).to_numpy(),
    })
```
